questions.q: What is the one mission a SOC's three core activities all serve?
options: Continuously monitoring, detecting, and responding to threats against an organization's systems and data
Writing firewall rules and nothing else
Selling security software to other companies
Running annual compliance audits only once a year
questions.explain: Monitoring, detection, and response are one pipeline, not three separate jobs — each depends on the one before it.

questions.q: Why is 'continuous' the operative word in a SOC's mission?
options: Attackers don't restrict themselves to business hours, so monitoring that stops at 5 p.m. leaves real gaps
It just sounds more professional in a job posting
Logs are only generated during business hours
Continuous monitoring is a legal requirement in every country
questions.explain: Off-hours, weekends, and holidays are exactly when attackers expect fewer defenders to be watching.

questions.q: In the 2013 Target breach example from this lesson, what actually went wrong?
options: Monitoring tools generated real alerts on the attacker's activity, but no fully staffed team acted on them in time
The company had no monitoring tools installed at all
The breach was caused by a tool malfunction, not a staffing gap
Customers' payment data was never actually at risk
questions.explain: The tooling worked — the gap was a continuous, staffed team positioned to act on what it found.

questions.q: Which of these is NOT one of the three real reasons this lesson gives for investing in a SOC?
options: Guaranteeing a company will never experience a breach
Regulatory requirements such as PCI-DSS and HIPAA
Reducing the overall cost of a breach through faster detection
Protecting customer trust and brand reputation
questions.explain: No SOC can guarantee zero breaches — the real value is regulation, lower breach cost, and trust, not a guarantee.

questions.q: Why would a SOC that only did detection, without response, fail to accomplish its mission?
options: An alert that's raised but never acted on doesn't actually stop anything from happening
Detection without response is technically impossible to build
Detection tools require a response team to even generate alerts
There is no real difference between detection and response
questions.explain: Detection only produces a signal — response is the step that actually contains and remediates the threat.
